lesson.title: Deleting by List Position
lesson.driving_question: How can a program delete a list item when it knows the position rather than the value?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Deleting a list item when its position is known
lesson.concept_budget: Use del with one valid position and contrast it explicitly with remove() by value.
misconceptions: remove() chooses by value while del chooses by position.
lesson.progression_note: Completes the core list-editing operations and prepares positional row deletion in 2D data.

shared_program.filename: Deleting by List Position - Starter Code.py
shared_program.code:
tasks = ["email", "design", "test", "publish"]
position = int(input("Completed position 0 to 3: "))
completed = tasks[position]
del tasks[position]
print("Completed:", completed)
print("Remaining:", tasks)

primm.prompt: Recall how indexing reads an item and how remove() deletes a known value.
Use position 2. Record completed before deletion and trace which later item shifts left.
Run with 2 and then restart with 0. Confirm the completed label always matches the item that disappears.

questions: Why is the item stored before del removes it?
What happens if del uses a position that does not exist?
How do later positions change after an item is deleted?
If you enter position 1, what are the exact Completed and Remaining lines?

primm.prompt: Keep the user-selected deletion. After it, display the new first task with the label "Next:". Test position 0; email must be completed and design must be next.
After the first deletion, ask for a second valid position in the shortened list. Label and delete that item, then display what remains. Test the program by entering 1 for both positions.
Build a queue editor with four names. Ask for one valid cancellation position, store and delete that name, then traverse the remaining queue with numbered positions using a counter.
Repair the square brackets and use del as a statement before displaying the shortened list.

concept_sheet.title: Deleting by List Position – Concept Sheet

blocks.definition: A statement that removes the item at a specified list position.
The zero-based index of the item to remove.
Later items move one position earlier after deletion.
Use del when the index is known.
Use remove() when the stored value is known.
